long_biography.plain_text:
Roman Abramovich converted control of Sibneft into a wider investment portfolio when he sold the oil producer to Gazprom in 2005. He had built a commodity-trading business before acquiring the company during post-Soviet privatisation. Steelmaker Evraz and nickel producer Norilsk Nickel became leading components of his subsequent holdings.

His public profile developed far beyond those investments. Abramovich served eight years as governor of Chukotka and directed substantial personal investment into basic infrastructure in the remote region. He also owned Chelsea Football Club for nineteen years, overseeing sustained success after football's unpredictability had drawn him to the sport during European business travel.
